Q: How to sort alphanumeric values in SQL Server properly A:

I am pretty sure this cannot be done too easily.

Your statement:

I'd like you to know that this field COULD be ANYTHING i.e.

pretty much kills it, otherwise one could have split alphabetic and numeric values in two columns or let them be split by some string-function.

But this way the only way out I could see is:

Write your own function that returns a numeric value by which you can sort. Then you can use it like this:

SELECT AlphaNumericValue FROM ValuesTable ORDER BY dbo.GETSORTVALUE(AlphaNumericValue)

This could be a dummy body for such a function:

CREATE FUNCTION dbo.GETSORTVALUE(@value NVARCHAR)
RETURNS INT
BEGIN
    DECLARE @dummyValue INT = LEN(@value)
    -- do something with your string here to get a sorting number
    RETURN @dummyValue
END

Since the values inside your column could be anything you would need to come up with a good sorting first, that should be included in that function then. For example you did not yet define how to sort in this case:

You say AAB 2 should come before AAB 10, but what about AA2B and AA10B?

Once you've defined this, your custom logic should go into that function.

Q: MySQL 'Order By' - sorting alphanumeric correctly A:

Just do this:

SELECT * FROM table ORDER BY column `name`+0 ASC

Appending the +0 will mean that:

0,
10,
11,
2,
3,
4

Becomes:

0,
2,
3,
4,
10,
11

Q: Order by alpha then numeric A:

My suggestion is to make the logic change to the calculation for rn. Then use rn for the ordering:

SELECT D.PRIO, D.REVISION,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY PRIO, (CASE WHEN REVISION IN ('0', '00') THEN 1 ELSE 2 END) DESC, REVISION ) AS RN
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT CONVERT(INT, LEFT(REVISION, PATINDEX('%[^0-9]%', REVISION+'z')-1)) as PRIO,
             REVISION 
      FROM DOCUMENTS
     ) D
ORDER BY RN

Q: Vectorized version of Brent's algorithm (root-finding) A:

This archive is 10 years old and i have created an open source vectorised root solver called rapid roots it. There is no need to re-implement Brent since it is already taken care of the library. REMEMBER to ensure the formula is numba compatible with @njit decorator. This example assumes that we are looking for d which is density in this case.

First install the rapid-roots library:

 pip install rapid-roots

Then you can easily use rapid-roots as follows:

from rapid_roots.solvers import RootSolvers
from numba import njit
import numpy as np

# Input the TE0S - 10 pressure function and ensure it is decorated with @njit

@njit 
def pressure_equation(d, t, p_target):
    """Returns f(t,d) - p_target so the root is the d where pressure matches"""
    return teos10_pressure(t,d) - p_target # EOS implementation

# This is the t and p values which changes for each problem
t_vals = np.array([...])
p_vals = np.array([...])

# func_params is the function parameters for each of the equation which is t and p in this case
func_params = np.column_stack([t_vals, p_vals])

# Bounds for density. This is just an example for this range but create it as you would.
d_lower = np.full(len(t_vals), 1000.0) # min example density
d_upper = np.full(len(t_vals), 1100.0) # max example density

# Use the RootSolvers to get the roots
roots, iters, converged = RootSolvers.get_root(
    func=pressure_equation,
    a=d_lower,
    b=d_upper,
    func_params=func_params,
    main_solver='brent',
    use_backup=True,
    backup_solvers=['bisection'] # Newton requires a derivative so it is not used for this example
)

d_solved = roots
print(f"Converged: {converged.sum()}/{len(t_vals)}")

This is how it should theoretically be used to solve this vectorisation problem. If need reference on how to use it please refer to the rapid-roots github: https://github.com/CianQuezon/rapid-roots

Edit: Updated the answer to fit more of the reviewers question and how to solve this particular problem using rapid roots as shown by one of the comments.

Q: Return all rows in a group having a particular value of a column in two latest records of this group A:

Since 11.1

You may use the nth_value OLAP function. Refer to OLAP specification.

SELECT A, B, C
FROM
(
SELECT 
  A, B, C
, NTH_VALUE (A, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY B ORDER BY C DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) C1
, NTH_VALUE (A, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY B ORDER BY C DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) C2
FROM TAB
)
WHERE C1 = 'PQR' AND C2 = 'PQR'

dbfiddle link.

Older versions

SELECT T.*
FROM TAB T
JOIN 
(
SELECT B
FROM
(
SELECT 
  A, B
, ROWNUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY B ORDER BY C DESC) RN
FROM TAB
)
WHERE RN IN (1, 2)
GROUP BY B
HAVING MIN(A) = MAX(A) AND COUNT(1) = 2 AND MIN(A) = 'PQR'
) G ON G.B = T.B;

Q: Select all records belonging to a client having a unique value in column B (value = P) A:

If there aren't any nulls in ColumnB you can use NOT EXISTS:

select t.* from tablename t
where not exists (select 1 from tablename where Name = t.Name and ColumnB <> 'P')

See the demo.
Results:

>  NAME | COLUMNB
> ----: | ------:
> David |       P
> David |       P
> Kevin |       P
> Kevin |       P
